name: MS-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's strong Republican lean (R+21 partisan baseline)
Incumbent Mike Ezell running with a large fundraising edge ($990K to $29K)
Prediction markets price Democratic win at only about 4%
No competitive polling or expert ratings to suggest a race
model.rationale: This Gulf Coast district leans heavily Republican, Ezell is a renominated incumbent with roughly a 34-to-1 fundraising advantage, and markets give the Democrat about a 4% chance. With no polls or expert ratings indicating vulnerability, the fundamentals point to a comfortable Republican win.
model.watch: Any late independent spending or polling showing Ezell under 55% would be the first sign the race is closer than fundamentals suggest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
South Mississippi's 4th District is a solidly Republican seat, and first-term incumbent Mike Ezell is running for reelection after easily securing his party's nomination. His Democratic challenger, Jeffrey Hulum III, has raised under $30,000, while Ezell has brought in nearly $1 million, giving the incumbent an overwhelming resource advantage. An independent candidate is also on the ballot but is not seen as a significant factor.

No public polling or expert ratings target this race, and prediction markets give Democrats only about a 4% chance of an upset. The district's strong partisan lean and the incumbent's financial dominance make a competitive general election unlikely, pointing to a comfortable Republican hold in November.
